content:
maya: quick q — I'm going offline for surgery tomorrow morning, and I own the /gen-feature rollout. If something goes sideways and someone needs to disable the feature quickly, who is allowed to flip the emergency flag? also, what exact steps should they follow so we have an audit trail?

alex: short answer: only people on the current eng-oncall rotation and the SRE rotation leads can flip the global emergency flag for hosted routes. we enforce 2 things: 1) change must be done via the control-plane API or Console (no local DB edits), 2) you must create/annotate an incident ticket and ping #incidents.

sam: where does the audit record live? is it in the control plane only or copied to our SIEM?

alex: audit goes to three places by default: control-plane audit log (Console > Security > Audit), an event to our Event Bus (kafka -> SIEM) with the raw payload, and a Slack event to #incidents with a short summary. retention: control-plane raw audit 90d, SIEM depends on compliance retention tier.

sre-bot: [incident-bot] Incident placeholder created: INC-2026-2346 (you can attach more context).

sam: can you paste the minimum command someone should run? want to document for the runbook.

alex: yep. minimal example (replace values):

```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.company/api/v1/flags/toggle
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OP_TOKEN"
  -H "X-Request-Id: $(uuidgen)"
  -H "X-Redwood-Operator: maya@redwood.com"
  -d '{"flag":"/features/gen-api","action":"disable","reason":"emergency rollback - high 5xx","scope":"global"}'
```

alex: IMPORTANT: include X-Redwood-Operator header (or use your token identity) so the audit record has the human. Console toggles add a comment automatically.

sam: good call. what about rollback guardrails? e.g., if we disable, do we need to also revert traffic routing?

alex: standard flow: 1) disable feature flag (control-plane) 2) verify reduced traffic/metric drop 3) if it's a model/capacity issue, trigger routing to fallback model via routing policy (Console -> Rollouts) 4) only escalate to infra redeploy if disabling flag doesn't stop errors. always attach an incident number to the change.

leah: tested this in staging yesterday. toggling the flag adds an audit entry like this (redacted):

```json
{
  "actor":"leah@redwood.com",
  "action":"toggle_flag",
  "flag":"/features/gen-api",
  "from_state":"enabled",
  "to_state":"disabled",
  "reason":"stress test failed canary",
  "request_id":"c4d2e7f0-9a2b-4d2e-b1f3-1234567890ab",
  "timestamp":"2026-04-11T14:02:31Z"
}
```

leah: that JSON is what gets pushed to kafka -> SIEM and also shows a compact entry in Console audit view.

maya: if I'm stepping down as oncall lead for the day, what's the handoff text I should leave so whoever steps in knows they can act?

alex: leave 3 lines in the oncall handoff: 1) which flags you own (path), 2) any current canaries + their thresholds, 3) your preferred escalation person (e.g., "if I don't ack in 10m, ping sam and @eng-sre-lead"). example: 

"OWN: /features/gen-api (canary 10% prod); CHECK: error rate > 2.5% or p95 latency +50ms; ESCALATE: sam then eng-sre-lead"

sam: do we require explicit approval for a flip if the owner is not available?

alex: if owner is unreachable and it's an emergency (prod outage impacting customers), oncall can flip immediately but must create the incident and call the owner later. if it's a non-urgent rollback request, wait for owner or eng-sre-lead approval.

maya: ok thanks — I'll add that handoff snippet to my shift note and point to the incident flow.

sre-bot: [audit] Flag toggle recorded: flag=/features/gen-api actor=maya@redwood.com action=disable reqid=c4d2e7f0-9a2b-4d2e-b1f3-1234567890ab

leah: also added a short checklist to the runbook: verify canary logs, run healthcheck endpoint, post in #incidents, then flip. saved to: https://console.redwood.company/runbooks/kill-switchs

maya: awesome. I'll update my personal runbook and drop the link in the handoff. :+1:
